task.title: Transfer tasks, projects, and reports to another team user

user_message.content: how to i transfer all my task, projects and reports to another user of my team?

status_update.description: Manus is working on your request

assistant_message.content:
Short answer: Manus has no "change task owner" button you can click per task or per project. What you actually need depends on which of two situations you're in — handing work to a colleague on the same team, or moving your whole account's data into the team. Here's the practical path for each.

## If you're already on the same team and just want a colleague to take over

There are three separate layers, each with its own mechanism.

**1. Projects (the reusable structure)**
Invite the colleague as a project member. They then inherit the master instruction and the knowledge base — the setup and context, not your historical output. One important caveat: they only see tasks *they* created inside that project. Your existing tasks stay private to you. Projects can also be used as folders, so first drag your loose tasks into the right projects to tidy the handoff.

**2. Individual tasks and reports**
Open each task → **Share** → choose **Collaboration** (not plain Share) → add their email. They get full history, can prompt Manus themselves, and can export every output. This is what effectively makes a report "theirs" in practice. Two things to know:

- Only the task owner consumes credits, so collaboration is free for the recipient.
- Only you can invite people; they can't re-share.
- If a task involves logged-in websites, sandbox cookies are cleared when the first collaborator joins, so finish authenticated work first.

**3. Files behind the reports**
Reports are files in a task workspace. To make them permanently available independent of your task, download them and drop them into the project's knowledge base, or sync them to a shared Google Drive / Notion location and transfer ownership there — Drive and Notion do support real owner changes at the file/folder level.

## If you're leaving the team, or the real goal is a true custody transfer

This is the only genuine "everything moves to another person" mechanism, and it's admin-driven:

1. A team admin goes to **Members → Deactivated** tab.
2. Finds your profile, opens the three-dot menu, selects **Delegate...**
3. Picks the active member who receives custody, chooses the role, confirms.

The recipient then sees your profile in their Profile Switcher and can access all your tasks and files, subject to the role assigned. Admins can reclaim at any time. Note that a deactivated profile is read-only and doesn't consume a seat — so if they need to actively continue the work rather than just read it, the delegated profile role should be **Member**.

## If you're moving a personal account into the team

Use **Settings → Data Migration → Migrate to Team** (the admin must have enabled *Allow members to migrate personal data* in Team Settings). This brings tasks, files and history across in one shot. Before you confirm, be aware of the terms:

- Migrated data becomes the property of the organization, and you may lose access if you later leave the team.
- Any active personal Pro subscription is cancelled, with a pro-rated refund to your original payment method.
- The migration is irreversible; your personal space is reset to a blank profile.
- If you migrate as *Deactivated*, the profile stays locked until an admin reactivates it.

## What I'd recommend

For a normal handoff inside an existing team, do it in this order: consolidate tasks into projects, invite the colleague to each project, add them as a collaborator on the specific tasks and reports they must own going forward, then move the deliverable files into the project knowledge base or a shared Drive folder. That gets you 95% of a transfer without touching account-level settings.

For anything that involves seat allocation, whether a delegated profile counts against your seat quota, or a profile migration that has already gone through, the Manus help center is the authoritative source: [help.manus.im](https://help.manus.im) — those are account-level decisions I shouldn't guess at.

If you tell me which case you're in — colleague handoff, departing member, or personal-to-team — I can walk you through the exact clicks for your workspace.

user_message.content: I need to zip up a project and transfer over to my personal account or to someone elses personal account. Can you do that for me and make it so with one click i can deploy this project

status_update.description: Manus is working on your request

assistant_message.content:
I can absolutely do this — but I hit a hard stop on discovery: this cloud sandbox is completely empty (no project files, no repo checkout), and your GitHub connector token is currently invalid, so I can't see your repos either. I need one piece of information from you before I can package anything.

Here's what I'll deliver once I know where the project lives:

- **A clean `.zip`** — source only, with `node_modules`, `.git`, `.env` and build junk stripped out, plus a working `.env.example`.
- **A one-click deploy path** built into the zip: `vercel.json` / `netlify.toml` with SPA rewrite rules for a static or frontend app, or a `Dockerfile` + `docker-compose.yml` + `deploy.sh` if it has a backend/database. Either way the recipient unzips and runs one command, or drags the folder into Netlify Drop.
- **A `README.md`** with the exact 3–5 commands, and a short `TRANSFER.md` covering what to change (env vars, database URL, secrets) so it works on a different account without your credentials baked in.

Two things I need to flag before we start:

1. **The GitHub connector needs re-authenticating.** The token in this session is rejected, so any repo-based export or push to `github@apartmentcorp.com` will fail. If the destination is your *personal* GitHub account, that needs its own auth anyway — a personal access token with `repo` scope is the cleanest way, and you'd paste it into the secure input card rather than chat.
2. **Credentials are the main transfer risk.** Any `.env`, API key, Supabase/Stripe/database string, or OAuth client baked into the project shouldn't travel in a zip to another person's account. I'll strip them and leave placeholders unless you tell me otherwise.

So — where does the project actually live?

Where does the project I should package live?

This sandbox has no project files and your GitHub connector token is invalid, so I can't locate it myself. Pick the closest option and include the link or file in your reply. Also tell me the intended destination — your personal account only, a teammate's account, or both — and whether it's a static site (HTML/React/Vite/Next static) or has a backend with a database. That determines whether I build a Netlify/Vercel one-click config or a Dockerfile + docker-compose one-command deploy.

options: A Manus WebDev project (I'll paste the project link)
A GitHub repo (I'll paste the repo URL)
Files on my computer (I'll upload a zip or folder)
A project inside another Manus task (I'll paste the task link)

assistant_message.content:
I found your likely candidates by scanning your task list. Before I touch anything, I need you to confirm which one — because how I extract it differs, and one of these routes modifies the source task.

The three projects that look like real codebases:

| Task | What it is | Where its code lives |
|---|---|---|
| **Property Portfolio Analyzer — OM Intake Portal** (also branded "GPC Underwriting Control Center") | LIHTC/HERA rent compliance + offering memorandum intake | Managed WebDev project, `/home/ubuntu/gpcportal` in that task's sandbox |
| **Replace Pick'em App Prototype** (NFL Sunday Picks) | Published at `nfl-sunday-picks.manus.space` | Managed WebDev project, live checkpoint |
| **OneSite & Yardi Reporting Portal** | Sign-in protected, database-backed, still mid-recovery | Managed WebDev project with managed MySQL |

One important constraint: **I cannot reach into another task's sandbox from here.** Each task's filesystem is isolated, so I can't just `cd` into `/home/ubuntu/gpcportal` and zip it. There are exactly two ways to get that code into my hands:

1. **Attach the WebDev project to this session** — binds the real project here so I read the actual source, checkpoint it, and zip it. Cleanest, no credits spent in the old task, and I can add the deploy files directly. I need the project's resource link or ID from the source task's dashboard for this.
2. **Ask the source task to export it** — I send that task a one-line instruction to commit and produce a `.zip` download link, then I pull it here and repackage. Works for any project, but it runs that task and spends a few of its credits.

Either way, the deliverable comes back to you as one zip with a README and a `vercel.json` / `netlify.toml` (static) or `Dockerfile` + `docker-compose.yml` + `deploy.sh` (if it has a backend), plus a `TRANSFER.md` listing every env var the new owner must supply. Secrets get stripped, never carried across.

Which project should I package, and which extraction route do you want?

I found three candidates in your task list: (a) Property Portfolio Analyzer / GPC Underwriting Control Center, (b) Replace Pick'em App Prototype / NFL Sunday Picks, (c) OneSite & Yardi Reporting Portal.

Route 1 — Attach the WebDev project here: I read the real source and build the zip directly. No credits spent in the old task. Needs the project link or ID from that task.
Route 2 — Have the source task export it: I send that task one instruction to zip the code and return a download link, then repackage here. Costs a few credits in that task.

Also confirm: is the destination your personal account, a teammate's, or both — and does the project need a backend/database to run, or is it a static front end? That decides whether I build a Vercel/Netlify one-click config or a Docker-based one-command deploy.
